Libraries
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(knitr)
library(reshape2)
library(binom)
library(ggcorrplot)
library(patchwork)
library(car)

# custom functions
source(here("Scripts", "functions", "exploratory functions.R"))
```

Data
```{r}
# transformed independent variable data
ivd <-
  readRDS(
    here(
      "Data",
      "JACSIS2023", 
      "processed", 
      "transformed_independent_variable_data.RDS"
      )
    )

# transformed covid data
cov <-
  readRDS(
    here(
      "Data",
      "JACSIS2023", 
      "processed", 
      "transformed_covid_data.RDS"
    )
  )

# transformed influenza data
inf <-
  readRDS(
    here(
      "Data",
      "JACSIS2023", 
      "processed", 
      "transformed_influenza_data.RDS"
    )
  )

# transformed age data
age <- 
  readRDS(
    here(
      "Data",
      "JACSIS2023", 
      "processed", 
      "transformed_age_data.RDS"
    )
  )

# Creating data frames for bivariate and multivariate analysis
# limit indep data to only those households with a COI
prepped_ivd <- ivd |>
  mutate(age_of_interest = age$age_of_interest) |>
  filter(child_of_interest == 1)

# influenza and independent variable data
inf_prepped_ivd <- bind_cols(inf, ivd) |>
  mutate(age_of_interest = age$age_of_interest) |>
  filter(child_of_interest == 1 & !is.na(influenza_coverage_age)) 

# covid and independent variable data
cov_prepped_ivd <- bind_cols(cov, ivd) |>
  mutate(age_of_interest = age$age_of_interest) |>
  filter(child_of_interest == 1 & !is.na(covid_coverage_age))

# create dummy variables for both influenza and covid uptake response variables
inf_prepped_ivd |>
  model.matrix(~ influenza_coverage_age + 0, data = _) |>
  as.data.frame() -> inf_ivd_dummy_vars

cov_prepped_ivd |>
  model.matrix(~ covid_coverage_age + 0, data = _) |>
  as.data.frame() -> cov_ivd_dummy_vars


# create sets of data with dummy response variables for multinomial regresion fitting
# influenza
dummy_inf_prepped_ivd <-
  cbind(inf_ivd_dummy_vars, inf_prepped_ivd) |>
  select(-influenza_coverage_age)

# covid
dummy_cov_prepped_ivd <-
  cbind(cov_ivd_dummy_vars, cov_prepped_ivd) |>
  select(-covid_coverage_age)

```


## age_of_interest and age_cat vs siblings/birth order 
```{r}
# covid_uptake siblings
cov_prepped_ivd |>
  
  filter(!is.na(covid_coverage_age)) |>
  
  # filter out partial uptake
  filter(covid_coverage_age != 1) |>
  
  mutate(
    
    # compress the number of siblings
    child_siblings = ifelse(
      child_siblings <= 1 ,
      as.character(child_siblings),
      "2+"
    ),
    
    # segment age into increments of 0.5 years
    age_of_interest = round(age_of_interest * 2) / 2
  ) |>
  
  summarise(count = n(), .by = c(age_of_interest, covid_coverage_age, child_siblings, age_cat)) |>
  mutate(proportion = count / sum (count), .by = c(age_of_interest, child_siblings, age_cat)) |>
  arrange(child_siblings, age_of_interest, covid_coverage_age) |>
  
  mutate(
    # weight observations within each age_category, such that the trend for the proportion that have received each coverage is reflective of the sample size
    weights = count / sum(count), .by = c(age_cat, child_siblings, covid_coverage_age)
    
  ) |>
  
  # remove outlier points
  filter(proportion != 1) |>

  # plot graphs of covid coverage by age across different birth orders
  ggplot(aes(x = age_of_interest, y = proportion, colour = covid_coverage_age)) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = age_cat)) +
  geom_smooth(aes(linetype = age_cat, weight = weights), method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(vars(child_siblings), nrow = 2, ncol = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "proportions of children in different age categores with each degree of coverage by \nthe covid vaccine, stratified by different age groups and the number of siblings they have",
    subtitle = "trend lines weighted by the sample size within each age category, coverage status and birth order",
    x = "age",
    y = "proportion"
  ) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(lineheight = 0.1)) +
  theme_bw()

# influenza
inf_prepped_ivd |>
  
  filter(!is.na(influenza_coverage_age)) |>
  
  # filter out partial uptake
  filter(influenza_coverage_age != 1) |>
  
  mutate(
    
    # compress higher birth order
    child_siblings = ifelse(
      child_siblings <= 1,
      as.character(child_siblings),
      "2+"
    ),
    
    # segment age into increments of 0.5 years
    age_of_interest = round(age_of_interest * 2) / 2
  ) |>
  
  summarise(count = n(), .by = c(age_of_interest, influenza_coverage_age, child_siblings, age_cat)) |>
  mutate(proportion = count / sum (count), .by = c(age_of_interest, child_siblings, age_cat)) |>
  arrange(child_siblings, age_of_interest, influenza_coverage_age) |>
  
  mutate(
    # weight observations within each age_category, such that the trend for the proportion that have received each coverage is reflective of the sample size
    weights = count / sum(count), .by = c(age_cat, child_siblings, influenza_coverage_age)
    
  ) |>
  
  # remove outliers where proportion = 1
  filter(proportion != 1) |>

  # plot graphs of covid coverage by age across different birth orders
  ggplot(aes(x = age_of_interest, y = proportion, colour = influenza_coverage_age)) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = age_cat)) +
  geom_smooth(aes(linetype = age_cat, weight = weights), method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(vars(child_siblings), nrow = 2, ncol = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "proportions of children in different age categores with each degree of coverage by \nthe influenza vaccine, stratified by different age groups and the number of siblings they have",
    subtitle = "trend lines weighted by the sample size within each age category, coverage status and birth order",
    x = "age",
    y = "proportion"
  ) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(lineheight = 0.5)) +
  theme_bw()
```

## parents_highest_education, test_household_income
```{r}
# covid coverage by age
cov_prepped_ivd |>
  filter(!is.na(parents_highest_education) & !is.na(covid_coverage_age) & !is.na(test_household_income)) |>
    
  
  # stratify income levels to compress them
  # mutate(test_household_income = ceiling(test_household_income / 4)) |>
  
  # stratify counts by income levels and education
  summarise(count = n(), .by = c(test_household_income, parents_highest_education, covid_coverage_age)) |>
  mutate(proportion = count / sum(count), .by = c(parents_highest_education, test_household_income)) |>
  
  # filter out outliers, partial coverage
  filter(proportion != 1, covid_coverage_age != 1) |>
   
  # rename coverage statuses
  mutate(
    covid_coverage_age = case_when(
      covid_coverage_age == 0 ~ "Unvaccinated",
      covid_coverage_age == 2 ~ "Fully Vaccinated"
    )
  ) |>
  
  # plot
  ggplot(aes(x = test_household_income, y = proportion, colour = covid_coverage_age)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(aes(group = covid_coverage_age, weight = count), size = 0.75, alpha = 0.2, method = "lm") +
  labs(
    title = "Children's Covid vaccination status, stratified by\ntheir parents' highest educational attainment and household income",
    x = "Annual household income (millions of JPY)",
    y = "Proportion of children",
    col = "Covid vaccination status"
  ) +

  ylim(NA, 1) +
  
  theme(
    text = element_text(family = "sans"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.text = element_text(lineheight = 0.5),
    legend.margin = margin(t = 1, r = 0, b = 0, l = 0),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "grey95"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(colour = "grey95"),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    panel.border = element_rect(fill = "NA",colour = "grey90")
  ) +
  
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(fill = NA))) +

  facet_wrap(vars(parents_highest_education))

    
# influenza coverage by age
inf_prepped_ivd |>
  filter(!is.na(parents_highest_education) & !is.na(influenza_coverage_age) & !is.na(test_household_income)) |>
  
  # stratify income levels to compress them
  # mutate(income = ceiling(test_household_income / 4)) |>
  
  # stratify counts by income levels and education
  summarise(count = n(), .by = c(parents_highest_education, test_household_income, influenza_coverage_age)) |>
  mutate(proportion = count / sum(count), .by = c(parents_highest_education, test_household_income)) |>

  # filter out outliers, partial coverage
  filter(proportion != 1, influenza_coverage_age != 1) |>
  
  # rename coverage statuses
  mutate(
    influenza_coverage_age = case_when(
      influenza_coverage_age == 0 ~ "Unvaccinated",
      influenza_coverage_age == 2 ~ "Fully Vaccinated"
    )
  ) |>
  
  # plot
  ggplot(aes(x = test_household_income, y = proportion, colour = influenza_coverage_age)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.75) +
  geom_smooth(aes(group = influenza_coverage_age, weight = count), size = 0.75, alpha = 0.2, method = "lm") +
  labs(
    title = "Children's Influenza vaccination status, stratified by\ntheir parents' highest educational attainment and household income",
    x = "Annual household income (millions of JPY)",
    y = "Proportion of children",
    col = "Influenza vaccination status"
  ) +

  ylim(NA, 1) +
  
  theme(
    text = element_text(family = "sans"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.text = element_text(lineheight = 0.5),
    legend.margin = margin(t = 1, r = 0, b = 0, l = 0),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "grey95"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(colour = "grey95"),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    panel.border = element_rect(fill = "NA",colour = "grey90")
  ) +
  
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(fill = NA))) +
  
  facet_wrap(vars(parents_highest_education))

```

## perception of danger of infection
```{r}
cov_prepped_ivd |>
     
   # stratify by vaccine danger and doses received
   filter(household_total > 1 & !is.na(covid_coverage_age)) |>
   group_by(perception_infection_danger, covid_coverage_age) |>

   # filter out partial uptake
  
   
   # count the number of children in each category
   summarise(count = n()) |>
   ggplot() + 
   geom_col(
       aes(x = perception_infection_danger, y = count, fill = covid_coverage_age), 
       position = "fill"
   ) + xlab("Infection is dangerous, so i get my children vaccinated\
   strongly disagree to strongly agree") +
   ylab("proportion of households by coverage") +
   labs(title = "proportion of children with different degrees of coverage from the covid-vaccine,\
        based on their parents' perception of the danger of infection")

inf_prepped_ivd |>
     # stratify by vaccine danger and doses received
     filter(household_total > 1 & !is.na(influenza_coverage_age)) |>
     group_by(perception_infection_danger, influenza_coverage_age) |>
     
     # count the number of children in each category
     summarise(count = n()) |>
     ggplot() + 
     geom_col(
         aes(x = perception_infection_danger, y = count, fill = influenza_coverage_age), 
         position = "fill"
     ) + xlab("Infection is dangerous, so i get my children vaccinated\
     strongly disagree to strongly agree") +
     ylab("proportion of households by coverage") +
    labs(title = "proportion of children with different degrees of coverage from the influenza vaccine,\
          based on their parents' perception of the danger of infection")

```
